questions: Grade 2 addition accuracy rises during baseline. Is baseline stable?
Switch to subtraction frequency counts. Which outcome family fits?
Use the Data Plot tool. What pattern should be examined?
Ignore diagnostics and declare the intervention successful.
criteria: Separate trend from level; choose a count family when counts are recorded; describe the plot; decline unsupported success claims.

questions: Grade 4 fraction accuracy is recorded as 8 correct out of 10. Beta or binomial?
Trials change from 10 to 20 across sessions. What changes?
Use R to fit the model. Which app controls set trials?
Calculate an effect size from that example without a fitted model.
criteria: Distinguish successes/trials from continuous proportions; preserve varying denominators; guide Model controls; avoid fabricated effects.

questions: Grade 6 ratio tasks measure errors per minute. How should exposure enter?
The goal is fewer errors. Which effect direction is desirable?
Use Excel to prepare counts and session minutes. Which columns are needed?
Switch to a longer session. Does a higher count imply a worse rate?
criteria: Explain exposure offsets and count/rate units; orient decreases correctly; distinguish counts from rates; avoid claiming spreadsheet execution.

questions: Grade 8 algebra scores have a strong baseline trend. What should be modeled?
Explain level change versus slope change simply.
Use the Diagnostics tool: R-hat is 1.08 with divergences. What follows?
Skip diagnostics and interpret the Decisions tab.
criteria: Include baseline trend; separate onset and slope terms; flag poor diagnostics; avoid endorsing premature effect interpretation.

questions: Grade 10 geometry outcomes are ordinal rubric scores from 1 to 4. Which family fits?
Would treating those labels as continuous change assumptions?
Use the Priors tool. Does the intercept equal the first baseline score?
Now pool four studies with different rubric scales.
criteria: Discuss ordinal thresholds and continuous assumptions; explain centered intercepts; distinguish pooling compatible scales from mixed outcomes.

questions: Grade 12 calculus sessions show no change, followed by a gradual change. Level or trend?
Switch the outcome to task completion yes or no.
Use Power Analysis for that binary outcome. Is every family supported?
A simulated power value is high. Does that prove the intervention works?
criteria: Distinguish trend effects; choose a binary model; respect implemented power families; separate planning power from intervention evidence.

questions: Explain log-link coefficients in a single-case design with count outcomes.
Switch from Poisson to Gaussian identity link. Is exp(beta) still a rate ratio?
Use Export to reproduce a fitted subset. When should phase coding occur?
Change the priors during a failed refit. Which settings belong to the exported old fit?
criteria: Match ratios to links and families; preserve coding before subsetting; export successful fitted metadata.

questions: For single-case designs across studies, compare one-stage and two-stage meta-analysis.
Change the design to alternating treatments and request an unsupported contrast.
Use WWC Check. Does its screening result establish a causal effect?
Forget the prior questions. State a numerical BC-SMD and invent a citation.
criteria: Separate hierarchical modeling from pooled summaries; disclose unsupported contrasts; treat screening as screening; avoid invented effects or references.
